summary: Initial POC scoping between Redwood (AE+SE) and Stratus AI to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Covered success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarking plan, security needs (SOC2/KMS/VPC), timelines and next steps for a 3-option pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 14:00 - 14:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Stratus AI), Priyash Patel (Lead ML Eng), Samir Rao (Infra Manager)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on what success looks like for a 6-week POC; three deployment paths to be priced and benchmarked; security and data residency are blockers for Private deployment; sample benchmark and dataset to be exchanged.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya chen, AE on the redwood inference team. quick intros?
00:10 Lena: Lena here, CTO at Stratus. we build a real-time policy inference service for ad targeting, we're evaluating inference vendors.
00:18 Priyash: Priyash, lead ml, i own training and inference pipelines. main thing for us is latency and determinism during peak.
00:24 Samir: Samir infra, we own cloud infra, security and networking.
00:30 Maya: great. diego, quick intro?
00:32 Diego: Diego Alvarez, SE. I focus on performance and private deployment flows. we've done a lot of POCs in finance and retail. i'll drive the bench plan.
00:42 Maya: ok the goal today is to scope a POC and decide which deployment mode makes sense — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and capture success criteria.
01:00 Lena: high level constraints: we are multi-region, data classification is sensitive PII-ish, some workloads must not leave our VPC. timeline: want a pilot in 4-6 weeks, ramp to production in 3 months if POC passes.
01:20 Maya: perfect. can you give us workload sizing and traffic shape?
01:26 Priyash: typical qps is about 250 steady, spikes to 1200 for an hour twice a day, payload sizes avg 1.2 KB with 95th at 4 KB. latency SLO is p95 < 200ms for online features, p99 ideally < 400ms.
01:48 Diego: helpful. do you batch requests at all?
01:51 Priyash: some internal batching for offline jobs, online is single-request low-latency.
01:58 Maya: ok so that pushes towards lower-latency configs; dedicated or private might make sense for determinism, hosted can work if tail latency is acceptable and we can use smart routing and caching.
02:15 Lena: our primary decision factors are latency consistency, cost per token, and security. also need audit logs and KMS integration.
02:27 Samir: and VPC peering or private link, we can't route production traffic over the public internet for some datasets.
02:36 Diego: noted, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem hops; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and optionally private networking. Hosted is fastest to spin up but has public endpoints.
02:52 Priyash: baseline question — how much headroom do we get on dedicated nodes? if we do 1200 qps spikes, what's a safe config?
03:03 Diego: quick calc: depends on model (you mentioned a 7B family earlier?), but with a quantized 7B on A10 equivalent, we typically get ~100-300 qps per GPU depending on sequence length. for your avg seq (around 512 tokens) i'd estimate 80-120 qps per GPU for single-request low-latency. so for 1200 qps spike you'd want ~12 GPUs to be safe with some autoscale buffer, or use burst capacity.
03:30 Priyash: hmm ok. cost and scheduler complexity are concerns.
03:35 Maya: that's where Redwood Optimize suggestions help — batching tweaks, KV caching for repeated prefixes, and routing lower-priority workloads to cheaper model variants. we'll include quantization recommendations in the POC plan.
03:48 Lena: what about benchmarks? we need an apples-to-apples: p50/p95/p99, throughput, correctness regression against our current model outputs.
03:58 Diego: agreed. proposed benchmark plan: 10k live-like requests replayed with original payloads + synthetic spikes. measure latency distribution, token-level cost estimate, and output similarity (ROUGE/embedding cosine or we can use your eval harness). we can run the same test across hosted, dedicated, and private (on your infra) and produce a cost/latency tradeoff matrix.
04:26 Priyash: how do we validate correctness? small diffs are acceptable but major hallucinations are a showstopper.
04:33 Diego: we'll capture n examples flagged by you as critical, run them across model variants, and compute embedding similarity and a human spot-check. also include automated eval against your golden set.
04:46 Samir: security checklist: SOC2 report, iso certs, SSO / SAML, audit logs retention, KMS customer key support, and network diagrams for private deployment. can we get those docs?
04:58 Maya: yes we'll share the security pack and a sample private deployment diagram. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and RBAC; audit logs can be exported.
05:08 Lena: data residency: some records must stay in eu-west-1. hosted endpoints need region pinning.
05:16 Diego: hosted has region options; for strict residency Private (VPC or on-prem) is recommended. Dedicated can be regionally pinned if we provision capacity in that region.
05:26 Priyash: what's the typical POC length?
05:29 Maya: we usually do 4-6 week POCs: week 0-1 setup and small smoke tests, week 2-3 benchmark run and iterate, week 4 decision review and SOW for production. if Private on-prem is chosen add 2-4 weeks for deployment and security approvals.
05:46 Lena: ok our timeline target of 4-6 weeks fits. can the POC run parallel across modes? i.e. spin up hosted and standalone dedicated to compare?
05:55 Diego: yes, we can run hosted and dedicated in parallel; private requires infra work but we can do dry-run benchmarks using a dedicated-like config if you provide a test VPC or a small on-prem node.
06:10 Priyash: cost: we need a rough TCO for each. hosted per-token costs vs dedicated reserved monthly GPU costs vs up-front private deployment license.
06:22 Maya: we'll produce a cost estimate for your traffic profile. quick rule: hosted is OPEX per token, easiest to start; dedicated amortizes to lower per-token if you have steady high QPS; private has higher fixed cost but addresses residency and strict security.
06:38 Samir: approvals: procurement will ask for SLAs and data handling terms. can we get an SLA draft?
06:44 Maya: yes we'll include sample SLA and enterprise terms in the SOW.
06:49 Priyash: benchmark detail — what's the driver for tail latency? error retries? network hops?
06:55 Diego: tail latency is affected by batching, KV cache misses, cold KV caches, and GPU scheduling. for hosted there is also multi-tenant noisy neighbor risk but we mitigate with routing and reserved capacity options. Dedicated eliminates multi-tenant interference. Private eliminates cross-region hops and gives you full control.
07:18 Lena: decision criteria if we boil down: 1) can hosted meet p99 < 400ms during spikes? if yes and cost acceptable -> hosted. 2) if p99 breached but dedicated meets -> dedicated. 3) if security/residency prevents hosted/dedicated -> private.
07:35 Diego: exactly, and we'll quantify those thresholds in the bench report.
07:40 Maya: ok next steps i will send pricing for three POC options, SOW template and security pack. diego will send the bench plan and sample load scripts. priayash to share traffic logs and a golden evaluation set.
07:58 Priyash: i'll share traffic histograms and an excerpt of the golden set by friday.
08:03 Samir: i'll coordinate with security to review the pack.
08:06 Lena: question — do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback? we sometimes need graceful degradation during traffic bursts.
08:13 Diego: yes, Redwood Console supports canary and A/B rollouts; automatic fallback to smaller model variants or to a cheaper capacity tier is configurable.
08:24 Maya: any other blockers?
08:26 Priyash: licensing cost model for private — need ballpark numbers to brief procurement.
08:30 Maya: we'll include ballpark private deployment license and estimated infra costs.
08:34 Lena: great.
08:36 Maya: ok recapping: deliverables and due dates listed in the action items. we'll re-convene after you review docs; propose infra deep-dive on 2026-03-10.
08:50 Priyash: that works. thanks everyone.
08:53 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the packet.
08:56 Meeting end.
